reason: The passage describes Moses receiving a divine calling while tending his father-in-law's flocks. Jethro (Yitro), identified as 'a priest of Midian' (כֹּהֵן מִדְיָן), represents the only clearly identified elite figure in this text. He is portrayed neutrally to positively—demonstrating understanding and granting Moses permission to return to Egypt ('go in peace'). While Pharaoh and the Egyptians are mentioned as oppressors, they are portrayed as antagonists rather than as elite figures deserving sympathetic treatment. No members of the elite are explicitly portrayed in an unfavorable manner in this passage.
